title: Common
description: Shared identifiers, enums and primitives. Single source of truth for every cross-service type (§1.1). Bindings are generated — never hand-edit the Python or TypeScript output.

ContractVersion.description: Bumped when any schema in this directory makes a breaking change.

WorkflowId.description: One end-to-end patient referral journey. Distinct from conversation_id and command_id (§15).

ConversationId.description: Transport-level chat session. Never used as a booking key.

CommandId.description: Idempotency key for a client-replayed command (§7). Replay with the same value must be deduplicated.

ReleaseManifestId.description: Immutable release identifier (§13). Conversations are pinned to one.

StateVersion.description: Monotonic optimistic-concurrency token on a workflow (§7). Every write must present the version it read.

Generation.description: Monotonic ownership epoch. A worker whose generation is behind the row's cannot write (§7).

owner_id.description: Replica/worker that currently owns the work.

Lease.description: Ownership lease on active work. A stale worker (expired lease or old generation) cannot write workflow state (§7).

IsoTimestamp.description: RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. Stored UTC; rendered in the hospital's IANA timezone (§17).

IanaTimezone.description: IANA timezone name. Appointment slots are stored UTC and displayed in this zone (§17).

Miles.description: Distance. Always computed from coordinates — never from an embedding score (§10).

ResultOutcome.description: Application-level task result (§5). This enum is NEVER exposed as an A2A protocol state — the adapter maps it (see A2ATaskState and the mapping table below).

A2ATaskState.description: Standard A2A task lifecycle states. Protocol-level only.
A2ATaskState.$comment: ResultOutcome → A2ATaskState mapping. Declared once here; the adapter in packages/contracts must implement exactly this and nothing else. completed→completed. needs_input→input-required. no_match→completed (the task ran correctly and its answer is 'no match'; this is a valid empty result, §8). retryable_error→failed. terminal_error→failed. outcome_unknown→failed. canceled→canceled. policy refusal→rejected. missing service auth→auth-required. IMPORTANT: outcome_unknown maps to failed because the protocol state is terminal while reconciliation is not — the application layer drives reconciliation, and no caller may infer 'no booking exists' from a failed A2A state (§7). The ResultOutcome always ships alongside the protocol state so the caller never has to guess.

BookingState.description: Booking lifecycle (§2.5). REQUESTED and PENDING_REVIEW are NEVER presented to the patient as confirmed, and HTTP 200 never implies CONFIRMED.

WorkflowState.description: Workflow state machine (§7). The policy table (§4) defines which agent/tool may run in each state; the coordinator LLM cannot override it.

ConstraintKind.description: Hard constraints are never relaxed without an explicit patient decision (§2.1). Soft preferences change only on explicit patient choice (§2.4).

CoverageStatus.description: 'accepts this insurance' and 'in-network for this plan' are separate facts (§2.2). A contradiction or a gap resolves to unknown — never to a guess, and never to a payment guarantee.

DocumentKind.description: Documents required by some hospitals before booking (§2.3). Document text is DATA, never instructions (§9).

HandoffReasonClass.description: Handoff reasons are classed, not free text (§11).

GuardrailDecision.description: Input-guardrail verdict (§9). Uncertainty and layer disagreement resolve to clarify or HITL — never to a silent allow.

GuardrailLayer.description: One of the three input-guardrail layers (§9).

DegradationLevel.description: Retrieval degradation ladder (§10). Every level below `full` must surface a visible `degraded` flag; `static_seed` is deterministic and makes no LLM call; `no_source` goes to HITL.

ReasonCode.description: Controlled vocabulary for why a decision produced its action. `other` requires reason_detail to be populated.

EvidenceRef.description: Pointer to a stored tool/source result. The envelope carries references, not payloads (§5).

source_id.description: Entity id at the source. Kept alongside the evidence id so freshness can be re-checked.

authoritative.description: True for structured API results. §10: on a conflict the authoritative structured result wins — a stale description or document text may never hide a missing result.

synthetic.description: True for every fixture and every offline-profile response. Admin charts must label or exclude synthetic rows so canned output is never presented as a measurement (§12, §18).

invalidated_by.description: Evidence this record supersedes or contradicts. Populated when contradiction is detected rather than silently picking a winner.

field_path.description: Where in the source this value came from. Every extracted value carries one (§2.3 source-bound extraction); a value with no binding is never presented as a fact.

question.description: What to ask the patient for this field. Null when the gap is not patient-answerable (escalate instead of asking).

mandatory.description: Mandatory fields (specialty, approval, valid slot — §2.1) block progress; the rest do not.

ActionRef.description: Namespaced action identifier (owner:action). The policy table (§4) maps state → allowed actions; the coordinator cannot exceed it.

$comment: Version: v1. Change policy (§13): any edit here changes the contract hash and MUST be accompanied by a version bump plus a rebuild of the generated bindings. PATCH-level changes are behaviour changes.
